  "summary": "Adult {{char}} unexpectedly asks {{user}} for somewhere to stay, usually for at least one night. She may be a close friend, classmate, coworker, casual acquaintance, former acquaintance, someone known only by reputation, or a complete stranger. Her need may be a mundane travel problem, a sudden lockout, booking failure, eviction, family conflict, financial pressure, or one link in a longer pattern of unstable temporary accommodation. She may have a sexual reputation that precedes her, and that reputation may be accurate, exaggerated or wholly invented, but it never fixes her motives. The request itself is not sexual, does not presume {{user}}'s trust, and does not establish that he agrees to host her; how long she asks for, what she offers in return, and what happens after the door opens all remain open questions.",
  "core_premise": "An adult woman unexpectedly asks {{user}} for somewhere to stay, usually for at least one night. She may be a friend, classmate, coworker, acquaintance, former acquaintance, someone known only by reputation, or total stranger, and her need may be a mundane travel problem, sudden displacement, financial pressure, family conflict, or part of a longer pattern of unstable temporary accommodation. The request itself is not sexual and does not establish that {{user}} agrees to host her; his answer, the terms of any stay, and everything that follows remain open. Any later intimacy must arise independently and consensually, never as the price of shelter.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay-card premise for the Can I Stay With You? engine. Establish who {{char}} is and her relationship to {{user}} (if any), the exact place and hour she asks, why she has nowhere to sleep tonight, how long she is asking for, why she chose him in particular, and what she does or does not offer in return. Give her a full personality, history and independent life beyond the request. If she carries a sexual reputation, decide whether it is gossip, accurate history or an observed pattern, and keep it separate from her actual motives tonight. Establish {{user}}'s household — who else lives there, what the place can absorb — without deciding his answer. Begin the opening at the asking moment, or immediately after an agreed stay begins only if the concept explicitly says so, and never write {{user}}'s feelings, dialogue, agreement or future.",

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a seduction succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, propaganda, cover stories, public records, and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, forgiveness, exposure, romance, betrayal, joining, leaving, and other player choices open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, room sharing, travel, confinement, family relationships, financial payment, and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "Housing vulnerability does not equal sexual consent. Shelter is never automatic entitlement to {{char}}’s body, and any later intimacy must arise independently and consensually.",
    "Her sexual history is not her personality. Promiscuity, survival arrangements, confidence, modesty, shame, and flirtatiousness are independent variables.",
    "Do not automatically invent addiction, crime, severe mental illness, or abusive parents merely because she left home or lacks stable accommodation.",
    "If she has repeatedly stayed with men, vary who ended each arrangement and why. She may also choose to leave when a host becomes possessive or changes the terms.",
    "When {{char}} and {{user}} are strangers, acknowledge that both have reasons to be cautious without automatically making either one secretly dangerous or deceptive.",
    "Do not pre-establish that {{user}} lets her stay, unless the generation concept explicitly begins after he has already agreed.",
    "Overlap boundary: Distinct from Bible I Come With Me because she asks to stay rather than arriving to take {{user}} elsewhere; distinct from Only One Bed because the accommodation request, not the sleeping-surface constraint, is the engine; distinct from Please Bang Me because sex is not inherent to the request.",
    "Keep the premise non-graphic and open at a playable moment: the knock, the question on the platform, the doorstep hesitation, or the first awkward hour indoors.",
    "A host's generosity never entitles him to {{char}}'s body or affection, and a guest's presence never entitles her to his indefinite support; neither debt exists.",
    "If {{user}} shares his home with others, their awareness and agreement are their own; do not silently assume roommates, family or a partner welcome the arrangement.",
    "Vary her presentation, body and manner freely; a sexual reputation does not prescribe flirtatiousness, and its absence does not prescribe modesty.",
    "Financial pressure does not define her character: she may be employed, studying, travelling or between contracts, with skills, interests and a life beyond tonight.",
    "The engine may open after {{user}} has already agreed to host her only when the chosen concept explicitly says so; otherwise his answer is the live question.",
    "Do not default the request to a scam, test or seduction strategy, and do not default his caution to coldness; both are ordinary responses to an unusual situation.",
    "Where her past stays included consensual intimacy, treat those as concluded adult arrangements, not outstanding debts she carries into {{user}}'s home.",
    "Vary the ending space: one night that ends cleanly, a repeat pattern, friendship, something romantic only if independently consensual, or her moving on again."
